::: justify-text
PHES-EF is being developed using an established, internationally recognized consensus methodology. The study follows its [published protocol](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0310342) and will be reported using the ACCORD guideline for consensus studies, with PRISMA-ScR for the scoping reviews and GRIPP2 for public involvement. This approach ensures:

::: method-points
- Evidence-based content through two systematic scoping reviews
- International consensus via a two-round e-Delphi survey and a consensus meeting
- Diverse perspectives from content experts, knowledge users and engaged members of the public
- Transparent development with open sharing of materials and progress on the [Open Science Framework](https://osf.io/8tcz6/)
- Broad applicability across public health environmental surveillance systems, using wastewater-based surveillance as an example
:::

The framework will be developed in five steps.

### Step 1: Establishment of the executive group

A multinational and multidisciplinary executive group oversees the development of the evaluation framework. The group brings expertise from various fields, including public health, infectious disease and epidemiology; environmental and physical sciences; mathematical sciences; social sciences; communication, knowledge translation and exchange; knowledge users; and an engaged public. 

The executive group is responsible for providing feedback on the framework development process (e.g., framework organization, completeness, additions, redundancy), supporting and advising working groups in their area of expertise, connecting the study to other related projects, recruiting e-Delphi panellists, participating in the consensus meeting, disseminating the evaluation framework, advising and/or participating in post-publication activities, and promoting the adoption of the evaluation framework among their professional networks. Co-chairs are also responsible for decision-making when the executive group cannot reach a consensus, leading executive group activities, and the overall framework development process. 

For more information about the members of the study's executive group, please visit the [Team page.](team.qmd)

### Step 2: Generation of candidate items

We are systematically compiling a list of e-Delphi candidate items through two scoping reviews, content analysis and extraction, and executive group consultation. The scoping review searches are being updated. See [Work to date](work-to-date.qmd) for progress so far.

You can view relevant scoping review registrations and publications on our [Documents page.](documents.qmd)

### Step 3: International e-Delphi survey

PHES-EF will use an e-Delphi survey, an online version of the Delphi method, in which panellists rate candidate items over two anonymous rounds with feedback between them [@tricco2018; @nasa2021]. Running the survey online allows panellists to take part from anywhere, across time zones.

Key dates are in the [timeline](#timeline) below. For details on recruitment, eligibility, rating and consensus, see the [Delphi study page](delphi.qmd).

### Step 4: Consensus meeting

In preparation for the consensus meeting, the study working group will categorize the remaining candidate items for consideration into a preliminary evaluation framework. This will include merging and/or modifying the remaining items based on gathered feedback from the e-Delphi rounds.

A hybrid or virtual consensus meeting will be held in September or October 2027, using the Surveylet Delphi survey platform, after the results of the e-Delphi have been compiled and analysed. The primary objective of the meeting will be to achieve expert consensus on the final list of items for PHES-EF, through review and discussion of salient items. This process will be guided by the empirical evidence that was identified during the scoping reviews, and the opinions gathered during the e-Delphi process. The secondary objective will be to discuss publication and dissemination strategies for the final evaluation framework.

Steps to produce the final list of items are as follows: (i) present the results of the e-Delphi exercise (name, rationale, and score of each item); (ii) discuss the rationale and relevance for including the items in the framework; and (iii) vote on equivocal and non-consensual items. PHES-EF will be developed based on the final list of items that receive consensus during the executive group consensus meeting.

### Step 5: Dissemination of evaluation framework

The development of the evaluation framework will be reported in a statement document that will include the rationale and a brief description of the meeting, and the panellists involved. While the publication strategy will be finalized based on the consensus meeting discussion, the preliminary approach will be to post to OSF, as a preprint, before submission to an open-access peer-reviewed journal in late 2027. During this time, we will actively seek feedback from experts, knowledge users, and the public within our networks and via social media. PHES-EF will be made available under an open licence [(CC BY-SA 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).
